# Results — Study 406 (Harami) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — detect every
**harami** (a small real body sitting fully inside the prior, larger, opposite-coloured
body) on daily bars across a fixed basket; confirm at the close, **enter the next open**
(one execution lag), and measure the forward **1 / 3 / 5 / 10-day** return **signed by the
pattern direction** (long after bullish, short after bearish) against the unconditional base
rate. As-of **2026-06-18** (the data's last bar). Basket: 29 long-listed liquid US
large-caps + **SPY** (yfinance daily, `auto_adjust=True`). Panel fingerprint: `bf1d6cb7ca54`.*

> **Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** The basket is names still trading in 2026; a
> fixed surviving-names panel cannot include firms delisted after a bad run. Here the bias
> works *for* a long-biased reversal claim (survivors drift up) — and the harami still fails
> as a two-legged reversal, so the verdict is conservative against the claim.

## Pooled signed return — long bullish / short bearish, gross (cost = 0)

| H | n | bull | bear | mean % | base long % | win % | HAC *t* | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* | net % |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 13078 | 6700 | 6378 | +0.020 | +0.028 | 50.1 | 1.65 | 1.64 | 0.051 | −0.081 |
| 3 | 13073 | 6699 | 6374 | +0.048 | +0.141 | 51.1 | **2.12** | 2.08 | 0.019 | −0.055 |
| 5 | 13071 | 6697 | 6374 | +0.099 | +0.253 | 51.3 | **3.39** | 3.24 | 0.001 | −0.006 |
| 10 | 13054 | 6686 | 6368 | +0.142 | +0.530 | 51.5 | **3.37** | 3.28 | 0.000 | +0.032 |

- Pooled, the signed return **clears the HAC *t* ≥ 2 bar** from 3 days out (and strongly at
  5/10 days). By the raw inference bar that is a positive Signal — but "pooled" hides which
  leg carries it. Net of costs the two-sided rule is ≈ 0 (net −0.006% at 5d, +0.032% at 10d).

## Leg split — the reversal is one-legged

| H | leg | n | mean % | HAC *t* | win % |
|--:|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | bullish (long) | 6700 | +0.075 | **+4.50** | 51.9 |
| 1 | bearish (short) | 6378 | −0.039 | **−2.15** | 48.3 |
| 3 | bullish (long) | 6699 | +0.198 | **+6.34** | 55.0 |
| 3 | bearish (short) | 6374 | −0.109 | **−3.31** | 47.1 |
| 5 | bullish (long) | 6697 | +0.337 | **+8.00** | 55.8 |
| 5 | bearish (short) | 6374 | −0.151 | **−3.38** | 46.5 |
| 10 | bullish (long) | 6686 | +0.652 | **+10.17** | 57.4 |
| 10 | bearish (short) | 6368 | −0.394 | **−5.81** | 45.3 |

- The **bullish leg** is strongly positive at every horizon. The **bearish leg is
  wrong-signed** at every horizon (a negative *signed* return means shorting the "top" loses
  money — the stock keeps climbing). A genuine reversal must work in both directions; this one
  only works on the side that agrees with the market's long-run drift.

## Alpha vs beta — the bullish leg's excess over the unconditional drift

Welch *t* of the bullish-harami long return minus the unconditional long forward return:

| H | excess Welch *t* |
|--:|--:|
| 1 | **+2.74** |
| 3 | +1.68 |
| 5 | +1.88 |
| 10 | +1.94 |

- Over the drift you'd get for free, the bullish leg clears *t* = 2 **only at 1 day**; at
  3/5/10 days it is below the bar. The multi-day pooled significance is mostly the market's
  upward drift, not a reversal — i.e. **beta in a costume**.

## Myth check (H = 1) — do the textbook confirmations rescue it?

| filter | n | mean % | HAC *t* | win % |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| plain | 13078 | +0.020 | 1.65 | 50.1 |
| + prior trend (down for bull / up for bear) | 7612 | +0.018 | 1.17 | 49.8 |
| + volume contraction on the inside day | 8830 | +0.018 | 1.31 | 50.2 |
| + both | 4863 | +0.001 | 0.06 | 49.6 |

The canonical "only counts after a trend, with a volume contraction" confirmations do **not**
lift the 1-day signal — both filters lower the *t*, and "+both" extinguishes it (*t* = 0.06).

## Costs

Each event is a fresh round trip: a one-way cost in and out (× NAV), plus 50 bps/yr borrow on
the bearish (short) legs over the holding period. At a realistic **5 bps one-way**, the 5-day
two-sided rule nets ≈ 0 (−0.006%); the thin gross edge does not survive.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's something to find

On a deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`), the same detector + inference:

| Planted day-after reversal `edge` | HAC *t* (H=1) | placebo *p* | win % |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.000 (null / random walk) | +0.06 | 0.479 | 50 |
| +0.004 (planted reversal) | **+37.73** | 0.000 | 62 |

The engine reads ≈ 0 on the null and lights up cleanly when a reversal is planted — so the
real-tape verdict is a statement about the **market**, not the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** Pooled signed HAC *t* = **3.39** (5d) clears the bar, but it is
  **one-legged**: bullish leg *t* = **+10.17** (10d) vs bearish leg *t* = **−5.81**
  (wrong-signed). Real on the long leg, busted on the short. *(Survivorship named: survivors
  tilt the long leg up; the verdict is conservative against the claim.)*
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of a 5 bps round trip + short borrow the two-sided rule is
  ≈ 0 (net −0.006% at 5d). The thin gross edge does not survive realistic costs.
- **Reliable reversal? — MISATTRIBUTED.** The bullish leg's excess over the unconditional
  drift clears *t* = 2 only at 1 day (Welch *t* = 2.74), fading to noise by 10 days — the gain
  is beta/drift, not a trend flip; the bearish leg fails outright.
